title: I Verbi Modali: Dovere, Potere, Volere
subtitle: Must, can, and want — the three modal verbs that pair with an infinitive.
objectives: Conjugate dovere, potere and volere in the present tense
Use modal verbs correctly with a following infinitive

content.intro: Dovere, potere and volere are Italian's three core modal verbs — each pairs directly with an infinitive to add a layer of meaning: obligation, ability/permission, or desire.
content.explanation: All three are irregular, and all three are followed directly by a bare infinitive with no preposition in between — a simpler pattern than English's mix of "must", "have to", "can", "is able to". With reflexive verbs and object pronouns (covered later), the pronoun can attach either before the modal or to the end of the infinitive: Mi devo alzare / Devo alzarmi — both correct.

rules.heading: a) Dovere — obligation/necessity
rules.body: Devo studiare stasera. (I have to study tonight.) Also used for probability: Deve essere tardi. (It must be late.)

rules.heading: b) Potere — ability/permission
rules.body: Posso aprire la finestra? (Can/May I open the window? — both ability and permission use potere, unlike English's can/may distinction.)

rules.heading: c) Volere — desire
rules.body: Voglio andare in vacanza. (I want to go on vacation.) A softer, more polite form is the conditional vorrei (I would like), introduced at B1.

examples.it: Devo lavorare fino a tardi oggi.
examples.en: I have to work late today.
We can't go out, it's raining too much.
They want to buy a new house.

examples.it: Dovete finire il compito entro venerdì.
examples.en: You [pl.] have to finish the assignment by Friday.

commonMistakes.why: Dovere is followed directly by the infinitive, with no preposition.
Potere never takes a preposition before the infinitive.
Tardi is an invariable adverb (late) here, not the adjective tarda — no agreement applies.

items.explanation: Io form of dovere is devo.
Tu form of potere is puoi.
Loro form of volere is vogliono.

items.prompt: You're asking permission to leave early: "___ andare via prima?"

items.explanation: No preposition between dovere and the infinitive.

summary: Dovere = obligation/probability; potere = ability/permission; volere = desire.
All three are irregular and pair directly with a bare infinitive, no preposition.
Potere covers both English "can" and "may" — Italian doesn't distinguish them.
